e-8938.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
e-8938.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u, \quad 
y=1+u^2, \quad
z=v^2
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2.$
e-8938.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u, \: 1 + u^2, \: v^2\big\rangle.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=2{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨1,\,2(1),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨0,\,0,\,2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,-4,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8940.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
e-8940.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle v^2, \: u-v, \: u^2 \big\rangle$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=-1.$
e-8940.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=-1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,-1) & =⟨0,\,1,\,2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,-1) & =⟨2(-1),\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-8,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=-1$ correspond to the point 

$$
\big( (-1)^2, \: 2-(-1), \: 2^2 \big) = (1, 3, 4),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,\,-8,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-3,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ 4\cdot (x-1)+(-8)\cdot (y-3)+2\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ 4x-8y+2z+12 & =0 \\ 2x-4y+z+6 & =0 \\ 2x-4y+z & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8941.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
e-8941.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x=u+v, \quad
y=3u^2, \quad
z=u-v
$$

at the point $(2 ,3, 0).$
e-8941.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u+v, \: 3u^2, \: u-v \big\rangle.
$$

First, notice that since $(2, 3, 0)$ lies on the surface, we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064857/assets/9a57281535511312d2fda6f388161fcd624354785d73d48954d10f9e7821653b.png)

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,6u,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,6(1),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,6,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,\,2,\,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-6,\,2,\,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z⟩ & =0 \\ (-6)\cdot (x-2)+2\cdot (y-3)+(-6)\cdot z & =0 \\ -6x+2y-6z+6 & =0 \\ -3x+y-3z+3 & =0 \\ 3x-y+3z & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨cos(v),1,sin(v)⟩ and r_v=⟨−u sin(v),0,u cos(v)⟩. At u=1, v=π/2, these become ⟨0,1,1⟩ and ⟨−1,0,0⟩. Their cross product is ⟨0,−1,1⟩, so option e is a normal vector.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,y=u,\,z=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2},\,1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2},\,0,\,1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations x=ucos⁡v,y=u,z=usin⁡v at the point where u=1 and v=π2.

a
 ⟨0,2,−1⟩
b
 ⟨1,2,−1⟩
c
 ⟨1,−1,0⟩
d
 ⟨0,1,2⟩
e
 ⟨0,−1,1⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In vector form, our surface has the equation

r(u,v)=⟨ucos⁡v,u,usin⁡v⟩.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(ucos⁡v),∂∂u(u),∂∂u(usin⁡v)⟩=⟨cos⁡v,1,sin⁡v⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(ucos⁡v),∂∂v(u),∂∂v(usin⁡v)⟩=⟨−usin⁡v,0,ucos⁡v⟩

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when u=1 and v=π2:

ru′(1,π2)=⟨cos⁡π2,1,sin⁡π2⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩rv′(1,π2)=⟨−1⋅sin⁡π2,0,1⋅cos⁡π2⟩=⟨−1,0,0⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where u=1 and v=π2 is

n=ru′(1,π2)×rv′(1,π2)=|ijk011−100|=⟨|1100|,−|01−10|,|01−10|⟩=⟨0,−1,1⟩.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
content.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,y=u,\,z=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
content.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2},\,1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2},\,0,\,1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

a
 ⟨2,2,−1⟩
b
 ⟨2,−2,−2⟩
c
 ⟨1,2,−2⟩
d
 ⟨2,1,3⟩
e
 ⟨1,−2,3⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨2,2u,0⟩ and r_v=⟨1,0,2v⟩. At u=1 and v=1/2, they are ⟨2,2,0⟩ and ⟨1,0,1⟩. Their cross product is ⟨2,−2,−2⟩, which is a normal vector.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=2u+v,\,y={u}^{2},\,z={v}^{2}
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}.$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u+v,\,{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨2,\,2(1),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(\frac{1}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations x=2u+v,y=u2,z=v2 at the point where u=1 and v=12.

a
 ⟨2,2,−1⟩
b
 ⟨2,−2,−2⟩
c
 ⟨1,2,−2⟩
d
 ⟨2,1,3⟩
e
 ⟨1,−2,3⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

In vector form, our surface has the equation

r(u,v)=⟨2u+v,u2,v2⟩.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(2u+v),∂∂u(u2),∂∂u(v2)⟩=⟨2,2u,0⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(2u+v),∂∂v(u2),∂∂v(v2)⟩=⟨1,0,2v⟩

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when u=1 and v=12:

ru′(1,12)=⟨2,2(1),0⟩=⟨2,2,0⟩rv′(1,12)=⟨1,0,2(12)⟩=⟨1,0,1⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where u=1 and v=12 is

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
content.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=2u+v,\,y={u}^{2},\,z={v}^{2}
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}.$
content.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u+v,\,{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨2,\,2(1),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(\frac{1}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x={v}^{2},\,y=2v,\,z=4u
$$

at the point where $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}.$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{v}^{2},\,2v,\,4u⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4u)⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨0,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨2(\frac{1}{2}),\,2,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,\,4,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations x=v2,y=2v,z=4u at the point where u=12 and v=12.

a
 ⟨4,2,2⟩
b
 ⟨−2,1,0⟩
c
⟨−8,0,2⟩
d
 ⟨4,4,0⟩
e
 ⟨−8,4,0⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In vector form, our surface has the equation

r(u,v)=⟨v2,2v,4u⟩.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(v2),∂∂u(2v),∂∂u(4u)⟩=⟨0,0,4⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(v2),∂∂v(2v),∂∂v(4u)⟩=⟨2v,2,0⟩

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when u=12 and v=12:

ru′(12,12)=⟨0,0,4⟩rv′(12,12)=⟨2(12),2,0⟩=⟨1,2,0⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where u=12 and v=12 is

n=ru′(12,12)×rv′(12,12)=|ijk004120|=⟨|0420|,−|0410|,|0012|⟩=⟨−8,4,0⟩.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
content.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x={v}^{2},\,y=2v,\,z=4u
$$

at the point where $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}.$
content.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{v}^{2},\,2v,\,4u⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4u)⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨0,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨2(\frac{1}{2}),\,2,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=\frac{1}{2}$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,\,4,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations x=1+eu,y=2−ev,z=1−eu−ev at the point where u=1 and v=−1.

a
 ⟨−1,1,−1⟩
b
 ⟨−1,e,−e⟩
c
 ⟨−2,1,2e⟩
d
 ⟨−2,2e,−1⟩
e
 ⟨−e2,e−1,−1⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The tangent vectors at u=1, v=−1 are r_u=⟨e,0,−e⟩ and r_v=⟨0,−e^(−1),−e^(−1)⟩. Their cross product is ⟨−1,1,−1⟩, so option a is a normal vector.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=1+{e}^{u},\,y=2-{e}^{v},\,z=1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v}
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=-1.$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨1+{e}^{u},\,2-{e}^{v},\,1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+{e}^{u}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2-{e}^{v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{u},\,0,\,-{e}^{u}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+{e}^{u}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2-{e}^{v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-{e}^{v},\,-{e}^{v}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨{e}^{1},\,0,\,-{e}^{1}⟩ \\  & =⟨e,\,0,\,-e⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨0,\,-{e}^{-1},\,-{e}^{-1}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ e & 0 & -e \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1} & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -e \\ -{e}^{-1} & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}e & -e \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}e & 0 \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,1,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

a
 ⟨−1,1,−1⟩
b
 ⟨−1,e,−e⟩
c
 ⟨−2,1,2e⟩
d
 ⟨−2,2e,−1⟩
e
 ⟨−e2,e−1,−1⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

In vector form, our surface has the equation

r(u,v)=⟨1+eu,2−ev,1−eu−ev⟩.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(1+eu),∂∂u(2−ev),∂∂u(1−eu−ev)⟩=⟨eu,0,−eu⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(1+eu),∂∂v(2−ev),∂∂v(1−eu−ev)⟩=⟨0,−ev,−ev⟩

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when u=1 and v=−1:

ru′(1,−1)=⟨e1,0,−e1⟩=⟨e,0,−e⟩rv′(1,−1)=⟨0,−e−1,−e−1⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where u=1 and v=−1 is

n=ru′(1,−1)×rv′(1,−1)=|ijke0−e0−e−1−e−1|=⟨|0−e−e−1−e−1|,−|e−e0−e−1|,|e00−e−1|⟩=⟨−1,1,−1⟩.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms that ⟨e,0,−e⟩ × ⟨0,−e^(−1),−e^(−1)⟩ = ⟨−1,1,−1⟩. This vector has zero dot product with both tangent vectors, verifying option a. The deliberately incorrect submission selected b.

content.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=1+{e}^{u},\,y=2-{e}^{v},\,z=1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v}
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=-1.$
content.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨1+{e}^{u},\,2-{e}^{v},\,1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+{e}^{u}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2-{e}^{v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{u},\,0,\,-{e}^{u}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+{e}^{u}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2-{e}^{v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1-{e}^{u}-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-{e}^{v},\,-{e}^{v}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨{e}^{1},\,0,\,-{e}^{1}⟩ \\  & =⟨e,\,0,\,-e⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨0,\,-{e}^{-1},\,-{e}^{-1}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ e & 0 & -e \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1} & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -e \\ -{e}^{-1} & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}e & -e \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}e & 0 \\ 0 & -{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,1,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u+v,\,y={u}^{2}v,\,z=v
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2.$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,{u}^{2}v,\,v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2uv,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,{u}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨1,\,2(1)(2),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨1,\,(1)^{2},\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-1,\,-3⟩.\end{aligned}

Question 5
?

Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations x=u+v,y=u2v,z=v at the point where u=1 and v=2.

a
⟨1,1,1⟩
b
⟨1,4,0⟩
c
⟨4,−1,−3⟩
d
⟨4,1,−3⟩
e
⟨1,−4,0⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In vector form, our surface has the equation

r(u,v)=⟨u+v,u2v,v⟩.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u+v),∂∂u(u2v),∂∂u(v)⟩=⟨1,2uv,0⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u+v),∂∂v(u2v),∂∂v(v)⟩=⟨1,u2,1⟩

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when u=1 and v=2:

ru′(1,2)=⟨1,2(1)(2),0⟩=⟨1,4,0⟩rv′(1,2)=⟨1,(1)2,1⟩=⟨1,1,1⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where u=1 and v=2 is

n=ru′(1,2)×rv′(1,2)=|ijk140111|=⟨|4011|,−|1011|,|1411|⟩=⟨4,−1,−3⟩.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
content.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u+v,\,y={u}^{2}v,\,z=v
$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2.$
content.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,{u}^{2}v,\,v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2uv,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,{u}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨1,\,2(1)(2),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨1,\,(1)^{2},\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-1,\,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: From 1+v=2 and uv=1, we get v=1 and u=1, also satisfying u²=1. The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨0,v,2u⟩=⟨0,1,2⟩ and r_v=⟨1,u,0⟩=⟨1,1,0⟩. Their cross product is ⟨−2,2,−1⟩, giving option a.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨1+v,\,uv,\,{u}^{2}⟩$ at the point $(2,1,1).$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(2,1,1)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}1+v=2 \\ uv=1 \\ {u}^{2}=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,v,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,u,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨0,\,1,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(2,1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,v,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,u,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨0,\,1,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(2,1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨1+u,\,2v,\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}⟩$ at the point $(2,-4,-3).$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(2,-4,-3)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}1+u=2 \\ 2v=-4 \\ {u}^{2}-{v}^{2}=-3\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=-2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,-2) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-2) & =⟨0,\,2,\,-2(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(2,-4,-3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,-2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,\,-4,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
content.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨1+u,\,2v,\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}⟩$ at the point $(2,-4,-3).$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(2,-4,-3)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}1+u=2 \\ 2v=-4 \\ {u}^{2}-{v}^{2}=-3\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=-2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,-2) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-2) & =⟨0,\,2,\,-2(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(2,-4,-3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,-2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,\,-4,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function r(u,v)=⟨u,v2,u2−v⟩ at the point (1,1,2).

a
 ⟨−2,1,4⟩
b
 ⟨−2,4,2⟩
c
 ⟨4,2,2⟩
d
 ⟨4,1,−2⟩
e
 ⟨−4,1,2⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The point requires u=1 and u²−v=2, so v=−1, satisfying v²=1. Thus r_u=⟨1,0,2⟩ and r_v=⟨0,−2,−1⟩. Their cross product is ⟨4,1,−2⟩, giving option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-v⟩$ at the point $(1,1,2).$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(1,1,2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ {v}^{2}=1 \\ {u}^{2}-v=2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨0,\,2(-1),\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,1,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
content.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-v⟩$ at the point $(1,1,2).$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(1,1,2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ {v}^{2}=1 \\ {u}^{2}-v=2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨0,\,2(-1),\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,2)$ is

$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u,\,(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

 at the point $(1,1,\sqrt{3}).$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(2,3,4)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v=1 \\ u=1 \\ (1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,1,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0,\,-(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨2(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,1,\,2(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,\sqrt{3}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨(1+(1)^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,0,\,-(1+(1)^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,\sqrt{3})$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & \sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,4,\,-\sqrt{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function r(u,v)=⟨(1+u2)sin⁡v,u,(1+u2)cos⁡v⟩,u≥0,0≤v<2π,

at the point (1,1,3).

a
 ⟨−1,3,2⟩
b
 ⟨−3,2,4⟩
c
 ⟨1,−2,4⟩
d
 ⟨−1,4,−3⟩
e
 ⟨1,2,−3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that since (2,3,4) lies on the surface, we obtain {(1+u2)sin⁡v=1u=1(1+u2)cos⁡v=3⟹{u=1v=π6.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u((1+u2)sin⁡v),∂∂u(u),∂∂u((1+u2)cos⁡v)⟩=⟨2usin⁡v,1,2ucos⁡v⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v((1+u2)sin⁡v),∂∂v(u),∂∂v((1+u2)cos⁡v)⟩=⟨(1+u2)cos⁡v,0,−(1+u2)sin⁡v⟩

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when u=1 and v=π6:

ru′(1,π6)=⟨2(1)sin⁡(π6),1,2(1)cos⁡(π6)⟩=⟨1,1,3⟩rv′(1,π6)=⟨(1+(1)2)cos⁡(π6),0,−(1+(1)2)sin⁡(π6)⟩=⟨3,0,−1⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point (1,1,3) is

n=ru′(1,π6)×rv′(1,π6)=|ijk11330−1|=⟨|130−1|,−|133−1|,|1130|⟩=⟨−1,4,−3⟩.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
content.problem:
Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u,\,(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

 at the point $(1,1,\sqrt{3}).$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(2,3,4)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v=1 \\ u=1 \\ (1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,1,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}((1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0,\,-(1+{u}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨2(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,1,\,2(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,\sqrt{3}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨(1+(1)^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,0,\,-(1+(1)^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,\sqrt{3})$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & \sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,4,\,-\sqrt{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function r(u,v)=⟨u+v,2u2+v2,v⟩ at the point (1,2,0).

a
⟨2,1,2⟩
b
⟨4,−1,−4⟩
c
⟨4,−4,4⟩
d
⟨2,−1,3⟩
e
⟨4,2,2⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The point gives v=0 and u=1, satisfying 2u²+v²=2. The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨1,4u,0⟩=⟨1,4,0⟩ and r_v=⟨1,2v,1⟩=⟨1,0,1⟩. Their cross product is ⟨4,−1,−4⟩, so option b is a normal vector.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,v⟩$ at the point $(1,2,0).$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(1,2,0)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u+v=1 \\ 2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}=2 \\ v=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2v,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨1,\,4(1),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨1,\,2(0),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,2,0)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,0)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-1,\,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u+v),∂∂u(2u2+v2),∂∂u(v)⟩=⟨1,4u,0⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u+v),∂∂v(2u2+v2),∂∂v(v)⟩=⟨1,2v,1⟩

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
content.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,v⟩$ at the point $(1,2,0).$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(1,2,0)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u+v=1 \\ 2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}=2 \\ v=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2v,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨1,\,4(1),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨1,\,2(0),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,2,0)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,0)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-1,\,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: At u=v=1, the surface point is (0,2,1). The tangent vectors are ⟨2,1,1⟩ and ⟨−2,1,1⟩, whose cross product is ⟨0,−4,4⟩. Thus the tangent plane is −4(y−2)+4(z−1)=0, or y−z=1.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,u+v,\,uv⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=1.$
after.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,1,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2v,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨2(1),\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨-2(1),\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-4,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=1$ correspond to the point 

$$
({1}^{2}-{1}^{2},\,1+1,\,1\cdot 1)=(0,2,1),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,-4,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+(-4)\cdot (y-2)+4\cdot (z-1) & =0 \\ -4y+4z+4 & =0 \\ -y+z+1 & =0 \\ y-z & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,u+v,\,uv⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=1.$
content.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,1,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2v,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨2(1),\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨-2(1),\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-4,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=1$ correspond to the point 

$$
({1}^{2}-{1}^{2},\,1+1,\,1\cdot 1)=(0,2,1),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,-4,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+(-4)\cdot (y-2)+4\cdot (z-1) & =0 \\ -4y+4z+4 & =0 \\ -y+z+1 & =0 \\ y-z & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: At u=1, v=3, the point is (2,9,6). The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨6,9,0⟩ and r_v=⟨0,6,2⟩. Their cross product is ⟨18,−12,36⟩, proportional to ⟨3,−2,6⟩. Thus 3(x−2)−2(y−9)+6(z−6)=0, or 3x−2y+6z=24.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨2{u}^{3},\,u{v}^{2},\,2v⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=3.$
after.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2{u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2{u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2uv,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,3) & =⟨6(1)^{2},\,{3}^{2},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,9,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,3) & =⟨0,\,2(1)(3),\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,3)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,3) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 6 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨18,\,-12,\,36⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=3$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2(1)^{3},\,1(3)^{2},\,2(3))=(2,9,6),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨18,\,-12,\,36⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-9,\,z-6⟩ & =0 \\ 18\cdot (x-2)-12\cdot (y-9)+36\cdot (z-6) & =0 \\ 18x-12y+36z-144 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+6z-24 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+6z & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function r(u,v)=⟨2u3,uv2,2v⟩ at the point where u=1 and v=3.

a
 3x−y+3z=24
b
 x−2y+z=4
c
 2x−3y+z=144
d
 x−2y+3z=12
e
 3x−2y+6z=24
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(2u3),∂∂u(uv2),∂∂u(2v)⟩=⟨6u2,v2,0⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(2u3),∂∂v(uv2),∂∂v(2v)⟩=⟨0,2uv,2⟩

Next, we evaluate these vectors when u=1 and v=3:

ru′(1,3)=⟨6(1)2,32,0⟩=⟨6,9,0⟩rv′(1,3)=⟨0,2(1)(3),2⟩=⟨0,6,2⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

n=ru′(1,3)×rv′(1,3)=|ijk690062|=⟨|9062|,−|6002|,|6906|⟩=⟨18,−12,36⟩.

Since the parameters u=1 and v=3 correspond to the point

(2(1)3,1(3)2,2(3))=(2,9,6),

the equation of the tangent plane is

n⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0⟨18,−12,36⟩⋅⟨x−2,y−9,z−6⟩=018⋅(x−2)−12⋅(y−9)+36⋅(z−6)=018x−12y+36z−144=03x−2y+6z−24=03x−2y+6z=24.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms the point (2,9,6) and normal ⟨18,−12,36⟩. The plane 18(x−2)−12(y−9)+36(z−6)=0 simplifies to 3x−2y+6z=24, verifying option e. The deliberately incorrect submission selected b.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
content.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨2{u}^{3},\,u{v}^{2},\,2v⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=3.$
content.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2{u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2{u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2uv,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,3) & =⟨6(1)^{2},\,{3}^{2},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,9,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,3) & =⟨0,\,2(1)(3),\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,3)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,3) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 6 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨18,\,-12,\,36⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=3$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2(1)^{3},\,1(3)^{2},\,2(3))=(2,9,6),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨18,\,-12,\,36⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-9,\,z-6⟩ & =0 \\ 18\cdot (x-2)-12\cdot (y-9)+36\cdot (z-6) & =0 \\ 18x-12y+36z-144 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+6z-24 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+6z & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function r(u,v)=⟨ucos⁡v,usin⁡v,u⟩ at the point where u=2 and v=π2.

a
 y−2z=1
b
 y+z=2
c
 y−z=0
d
 2y+z=−2
e
 x+y−z=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The surface point is (0,2,2). At u=2 and v=π/2, the tangent vectors are r_u=⟨0,1,1⟩ and r_v=⟨−2,0,0⟩. Their cross product is ⟨0,−2,2⟩, so the tangent plane is −2(y−2)+2(z−2)=0, equivalent to y−z=0.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
after.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$

$$
(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2)=(0,2,2),
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,-2,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-2,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+(-2)\cdot (y-2)+2\cdot (z-2) & =0 \\ -2y+2z & =0 \\ y-z & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function r(u,v)=⟨ucos⁡v,usin⁡v,u⟩ at the point where u=2 and v=π2.

a
 y−2z=1
b
 y+z=2
c
 y−z=0
d
 2y+z=−2
e
 x+y−z=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(ucos⁡v),∂∂u(usin⁡v),∂∂u(u)⟩=⟨cos⁡v,sin⁡v,1⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(ucos⁡v),∂∂v(usin⁡v),∂∂v(u)⟩=⟨−usin⁡v,ucos⁡v,0⟩

Next, we evaluate these vectors when u=2 and v=π2:

ru′(2,π2)=⟨cos⁡(π2),sin⁡(π2),1⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩rv′(2,π2)=⟨−2sin⁡(π2),2cos⁡(π2),0⟩=⟨−2,0,0⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

n=ru′(2,π2)×rv′(2,π2)=|ijk011−200|=⟨|1100|,−|01−20|,|01−20|⟩=⟨0,−2,2⟩.

Since the parameters u=2 and v=π2 correspond to the point

(2cos⁡(π2),2sin⁡(π2),2)=(0,2,2),

the equation of the tangent plane is

n⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0⟨0,−2,2⟩⋅⟨x,y−2,z−2⟩=00⋅x+(−2)⋅(y−2)+2⋅(z−2)=0−2y+2z=0y−z=0.

$$

$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2)=(0,2,2),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$

$$

a

b

decision.explanation: At u=2 and v=6, the point is (2,6,−4). The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨1,0,3u²−v⟩=⟨1,0,6⟩ and r_v=⟨0,1,−u⟩=⟨0,1,−2⟩. Their cross product is ⟨−6,2,1⟩. Thus −6(x−2)+2(y−6)+(z+4)=0, equivalent to 6x−2y−z=4.

after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,{u}^{3}-uv⟩$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=6.$
after.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}-uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3{u}^{2}-v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}-uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,6) & =⟨1,\,0,\,3(2)^{2}-6⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,6⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,6) & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,6)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,6) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=6$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2,\,6,\,{2}^{3}-(2)(6))=(2,6,-4),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-6,\,2,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-6,\,z+4⟩ & =0 \\ (-6)\cdot (x-2)+2\cdot (y-6)+1\cdot (z+4) & =0 \\ -6x+2y+z+4 & =0 \\ 6x-2y-z & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters u=2 and v=6 correspond to the point

(2,6,23−(2)(6))=(2,6,−4),

Question 15
?

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function r(u,v)=⟨2u,usin⁡v,4u2⟩ at the point where u=1 and v=π.

a
2x−z=0
b
4x−z=4
c
8x−y−2z=8
d
8x+y−2z=3
e
x−4z=1
Submit

decision.explanation: At u=1 and v=π, the point is (2,0,4). The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨2,0,8⟩ and r_v=⟨0,−1,0⟩. Their cross product is ⟨8,0,−2⟩, so the tangent plane is 8(x−2)−2(z−4)=0, simplifying to 4x−z=4.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨2u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,4{u}^{2}⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\pi .$
after.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4{u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,8u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4{u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),\,8(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,8⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨0,\,(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,0,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=\pi $ correspond to the point 

$$
(2(1),\,(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),\,4(1)^{2})=(2,0,4),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨8,\,0,\,-2⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ 8\cdot (x-2)+0\cdot y+(-2)\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ 8x-2z-8 & =0 \\ 4x-z & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

b

c

d

Correct
EXPLANATION

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(2u),∂∂u(usin⁡v),∂∂u(4u2)⟩=⟨2,sin⁡v,8u⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(2u),∂∂v(usin⁡v),∂∂v(4u2)⟩=⟨0,ucos⁡v,0⟩

Next, we evaluate these vectors when u=1 and v=π:

ru′(1,π)=⟨2,sin⁡(π),8(1)⟩=⟨2,0,8⟩rv′(1,π)=⟨0,(1)cos⁡(π),0⟩=⟨0,−1,0⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

n=ru′(1,π)×rv′(1,π)=|ijk2080−10|=⟨|08−10|,−|2800|,|200−1|⟩=⟨8,0,−2⟩.

Since the parameters u=1 and v=π correspond to the point

(2(1),(1)sin⁡(π),4(1)2)=(2,0,4),

the equation of the tangent plane is

n⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0⟨8,0,−2⟩⋅⟨x−2,y,z−4⟩=08⋅(x−2)+0⋅y+(−2)⋅(z−4)=08x−2z−8=04x−z=4.

$$

$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),\,8(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,8⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨0,\,(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,0,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
(2(1),\,(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),\,4(1)^{2})=(2,0,4),

$$

decision.explanation: Since u≥0 and u²=1, u=1. The point requires sin(v)=0 and cos(v)=1, so v=0. The tangent vectors are ⟨2,0,1⟩ and ⟨0,2,0⟩, whose cross product is ⟨−2,0,4⟩. The tangent plane is −2(x−1)+4(z−1)=0, equivalent to x−2z=−1.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y=2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,z=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

at the point $(1,0,1).$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi .
$$

First, notice that since $(1,0,1)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}=1 \\ 2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨2(1),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨0,\,2(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,0)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,0,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2,\,0,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ (-2)\cdot (x-1)+0\cdot y+4\cdot (z-1) & =0 \\ -2x+4z-2 & =0 \\ -x+2z-1 & =0 \\ x-2z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,y=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,z=v
$$

at the point $(-2,0,\pi ).$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,v⟩.
$$

First, notice that since $(-2,0,\pi )$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-2 \\ u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ v=\pi \end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=2 \\ v=\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=2$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\pi ) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x+2,\,y,\,z-\pi ⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot (x+2)+1\cdot y+2\cdot (z-\pi ) & =0 \\ y+2z-2\pi  & =0 \\ y+2z & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-2 \\ u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ v=\pi \end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=2 \\ v=\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1⟩\end{aligned}

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=2$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\pi ) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2,\,1⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

decision.explanation: The nonnegative parameters are u=1 and v=2. The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨2,0,2⟩ and r_v=⟨0,4,1⟩, whose cross product is ⟨−8,−2,8⟩. Using the proportional normal ⟨4,1,−4⟩, the plane is 4(x−1)+(y−4)−4(z−2)=0, or 4x+y−4z=0.

after.name: Question 18
after.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y={v}^{2},\,z=uv,\,u\ge 0,\,v\ge 0,
$$

at the point $(1,4,2).$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,uv⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,v\ge 0.
$$

First, notice that since $(1,4,2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}=1 \\ {v}^{2}=4 \\ uv=2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨2(1),\,0,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨0,\,2(2),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,4,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,\,-2,\,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-8,\,-2,\,8⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-4,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ (-8)\cdot (x-1)+(-2)\cdot (y-4)+8\cdot (z-2) & =0 \\ -8x-2y+8z & =0 \\ 4x+y-4z & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
content.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y={v}^{2},\,z=uv,\,u\ge 0,\,v\ge 0,
$$

at the point $(1,4,2).$
content.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,uv⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,v\ge 0.
$$

First, notice that since $(1,4,2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}=1 \\ {v}^{2}=4 \\ uv=2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨2(1),\,0,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨0,\,2(2),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,4,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,\,-2,\,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-8,\,-2,\,8⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-4,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ (-8)\cdot (x-1)+(-2)\cdot (y-4)+8\cdot (z-2) & =0 \\ -8x-2y+8z & =0 \\ 4x+y-4z & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The equations u²=4, v²=1, and u+2v=4 give u=2, v=1. The tangent vectors are ⟨4,0,1⟩ and ⟨0,2,2⟩, whose cross product is ⟨−2,−8,8⟩. Using the proportional normal ⟨1,4,−4⟩, the plane is (x−4)+4(y−1)−4(z−4)=0, or x+4y−4z=−8.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y={v}^{2},\,z=u+2v
$$

at the point $(4,1,4).$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,u+2v⟩.
$$

First, notice that since $(4,1,4)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}=4 \\ {v}^{2}=1 \\ u+2v=4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=2 \\ v=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=2$ and $v=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,1) & =⟨2(2),\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,1) & =⟨0,\,2(1),\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-8,\,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2,\,-8,\,8⟩\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y-1,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ (-2)\cdot (x-4)+(-8)\cdot (y-1)+8\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ -2x-8y+8z-16 & =0 \\ -x-4y+4z-8 & =0 \\ x+4y-4z & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations x=u2,y=v2,z=u+2v at the point (4,1,4).

a
x+4y−4z=−8
b
x−4y+2z=8
c
2x+y−2z=−4
d
2x+y=4
e
x+2y=8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In vector form, our surface has the equation

r(u,v)=⟨u2,v2,u+2v⟩.

First, notice that since (4,1,4) lies on the surface, we obtain {u2=4v2=1u+2v=4⟹{u=2v=1.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u2),∂∂u(v2),∂∂u(u+2v)⟩=⟨2u,0,1⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u2),∂∂v(v2),∂∂v(u+2v)⟩=⟨0,2v,2⟩

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when u=2 and v=1:

ru′(2,1)=⟨2(2),0,1⟩=⟨4,0,1⟩rv′(2,1)=⟨0,2(1),2⟩=⟨0,2,2⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

n=ru′(2,1)×rv′(2,1)=|ijk401022|=⟨|0122|,−|4102|,|4002|⟩=⟨−2,−8,8⟩.

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

n⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0⟨−2,−8,8⟩⋅⟨x−4,y−1,z−4⟩=0(−2)⋅(x−4)+(−8)⋅(y−1)+8⋅(z−4)=0−2x−8y+8z−16=0−x−4y+4z−8=0x+4y−4z=−8.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
content.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y={v}^{2},\,z=u+2v
$$

at the point $(4,1,4).$
content.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,u+2v⟩.
$$

First, notice that since $(4,1,4)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}=4 \\ {v}^{2}=1 \\ u+2v=4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=2 \\ v=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=2$ and $v=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,1) & =⟨2(2),\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,1) & =⟨0,\,2(1),\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-8,\,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2,\,-8,\,8⟩\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y-1,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ (-2)\cdot (x-4)+(-8)\cdot (y-1)+8\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ -2x-8y+8z-16 & =0 \\ -x-4y+4z-8 & =0 \\ x+4y-4z & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations x=usin⁡v,y=u2,z=2ucos⁡v,u≥0,0≤v<2π, at the point (0,1,−2).

a
y−2z=2
b
y+z=−1
c
2y−2z=1
d
x−2z=1
e
x+z=2
Submit

decision.explanation: The point and parameter restrictions give u=1 and v=π. The tangent vectors are r_u=⟨0,2,−2⟩ and r_v=⟨−1,0,0⟩, whose cross product is ⟨0,2,2⟩. Thus the tangent plane is 2(y−1)+2(z+2)=0, or y+z=−1.

after.name: Question 20
after.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,y={u}^{2},\,z=2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

at the point $(0,1,-2).$
after.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2},\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi .
$$

First, notice that since $(0,1,-2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ {u}^{2}=1 \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0,\,-2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,2(1),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨1\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,0,\,-2(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-1,\,z+2⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+2\cdot (y-1)+2\cdot (z+2) & =0 \\ 2y+2z+2 & =0 \\ y+z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations x=usin⁡v,y=u2,z=2ucos⁡v,u≥0,0≤v<2π, at the point (0,1,−2).

a
y−2z=2
b
y+z=−1
c
2y−2z=1
d
x−2z=1
e
x+z=2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In vector form, our surface has the equation

r(u,v)=⟨usin⁡v,u2,2ucos⁡u⟩,u≥0,0≤v<2π.

First, notice that since (0,1,−2) lies on the surface, we obtain {usin⁡v=0u2=12ucos⁡v=−2⟹{u=1v=π.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(usin⁡v),∂∂u(u2),∂∂u(2ucos⁡v)⟩=⟨sin⁡v,2u,2cos⁡v⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(usin⁡v),∂∂v(u2),∂∂v(2ucos⁡v)⟩=⟨ucos⁡v,0,−2usin⁡v⟩

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when u=1 and v=π:

ru′(1,π)=⟨sin⁡π,2(1),2cos⁡π⟩=⟨0,2,−2⟩rv′(1,π)=⟨1cos⁡π,0,−2(1)sin⁡π⟩=⟨−1,0,0⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

n=ru′(1,π)×rv′(1,π)=|ijk02−2−100|=⟨|2−200|,−|0−2−10|,|02−10|⟩=⟨0,2,2⟩.

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

n⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0⟨0,2,2⟩⋅⟨x,y−1,z+2⟩=00⋅x+2⋅(y−1)+2⋅(z+2)=02y+2z+2=0y+z=−1.

content.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,y={u}^{2},\,z=2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

at the point $(0,1,-2).$
content.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2},\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi .
$$

First, notice that since $(0,1,-2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ {u}^{2}=1 \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0,\,-2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,2(1),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨1\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,0,\,-2(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,2,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-1,\,z+2⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+2\cdot (y-1)+2\cdot (z+2) & =0 \\ 2y+2z+2 & =0 \\ y+z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
